banner: 一周三款开源旗舰，瓶颈转向算力
banner_en: Three open-weight flagships in a week; the bottleneck shifts to compute

image.caption: 开源旗舰的参数量赛跑,一张画完就得重画。Latent Space 追踪的开源最大模型:7 月 16 日还是 Moonshot 的 Kimi K3(2.8T)领跑,后面跟着 DeepSeek 1.6T、小米 1.02T、Thinking Machines 的 Inkling 975B。可就在本报截稿这几天,阿里又开出 2.4T 的 Qwen 3.8,而 Kimi K3 的需求已经猛到 Moonshot 停售新订阅。参数在涨,能供上的算力才是真门槛。(图:Latent Space《AINews:Kimi K3 2.8T-A50B》)
image.caption_en: The open-weight parameter race — a chart obsolete the moment it's drawn. Latent Space's tracker of the largest open models: on July 16 Moonshot's Kimi K3 (2.8T) led, with DeepSeek at 1.6T, Xiaomi 1.02T, and Thinking Machines' Inkling at 975B behind. Days later Alibaba opened the 2.4T Qwen 3.8, while demand for Kimi K3 grew fierce enough that Moonshot paused new subscriptions. The parameter counts climb; serving capacity is the real gate. (Chart: Latent Space, “AINews: Kimi K3 2.8T-A50B.”)

actions.text: 今晚给你最常跑的那个 agent 量一次上下文。OpenAI 刚把 Codex 的上下文从 372k 砍到 272k,HN 上的共识是这是成本和延迟的取舍,不是能力问题;还有人吐槽 Codex 到 10-20% 就自动压缩,真正可用的其实只有八成左右。挑你用得最勤的那个 agent,看它每一轮到底塞进去多少 token,有多少是重复的死重(整份 README、整棵目录树、翻来覆去的历史)。把上下文当预算管:能压的压,能分段的分段,该丢的丢。省下的既是钱,也是它的注意力。
actions.source: Hacker News · OpenAI reduces Codex context 372k→272k
actions.text_en: Tonight, measure the context on the agent you run most. OpenAI just cut Codex's context from 372k to 272k, and the HN consensus is that this is a cost/latency tradeoff, not a capability one; some also gripe that Codex auto-compacts as early as 10–20%, leaving only about 80% actually usable. Take your most-used agent and look at how many tokens it stuffs in per turn and how much is duplicated dead weight (whole READMEs, the entire file tree, history rehashed over and over). Manage context like a budget: compact what you can, chunk what you can, drop what you don't need. What you save is both money and its attention.
actions.source_en: Hacker News · OpenAI reduces Codex context 372k→272k

actions.text: 给自己立一条『先答再问』的规矩。三所欧洲高校做了个实验:能随手问 AI 时,人的答题准确率从 27% 掉到 9%,自信却从 30% 涨到 76%,愿意说『不知道』的从 44% 崩到 3%。有人在 HN 上点出,这实验是刻意用 AI 常答错的题设计的,所以别把它当成放之四海的准确率结论;但那个行为效应是真的:一个永远给答案的工具,会顺手把你的『不知道』删掉。对任何带判断或品味的决定,先花一分钟写下你自己的答案和几成把握,再去问 AI,然后比两边差在哪。这既挡住了那个效应,也帮你攒下一批能复盘的判断。
actions.source: Hacker News · AI advice made people less accurate but more confident
actions.text_en: Set yourself an “answer first, then ask” rule. Three European universities ran an experiment: with AI on hand, accuracy dropped from 27% to 9%, confidence rose from 30% to 76%, and willingness to say “I don't know” collapsed from 44% to 3%. Someone on HN rightly notes the study deliberately used questions AI usually gets wrong, so don't read it as a universal accuracy verdict — but the behavioral effect is real: a tool that always emits an answer quietly deletes your “I don't know.” For any call with judgment or taste in it, spend a minute writing your own answer and how sure you are before you ask AI, then see where the two differ. It blocks the effect and banks a set of judgment calls you can review later.
actions.source_en: Hacker News · AI advice made people less accurate but more confident

actions.text: 花 15 分钟给自己接一条开源『备胎』路由。Moonshot 因为 Kimi K3 需求太猛停了新订阅,HN 上一句话说透了开源权重的真价值:哪怕某一家实验室排队排到宕机,你还能从别的推理商或自己的机器上拿到 token。今晚去 OpenRouter 建个 key,把一个当下靠谱的开源权重模型(Qwen / GLM / Kimi / DeepSeek 家族任选)配成你主力闭源模型的 fallback,拿一条真实任务两边各跑一遍,确认它真能顶上。别等主力宕了那天,才发现自己没有二线。
actions.source: Hacker News · Moonshot AI suspends new subscriptions
actions.text_en: Spend 15 minutes wiring yourself an open-weight “spare” route. Moonshot paused new subscriptions because Kimi K3 demand outran its servers, and one HN line nails the real value of open weights: even if a single lab's queue backs up to the point of downtime, you can still get tokens from another inference provider or your own hardware. Tonight, create an OpenRouter key, set a currently-solid open-weight model (any of the Qwen / GLM / Kimi / DeepSeek families) as a fallback to your primary closed model, and run one real task through both to confirm it can actually take over. Don't discover you have no second line on the day your primary goes down.
actions.source_en: Hacker News · Moonshot AI suspends new subscriptions

hands_on.title: 今晚 15 分钟:把同一条任务在『低努力』和『高努力』各跑一遍
hands_on.why: Raschka 刚写清楚:推理努力现在是发布即带的一等旋钮,大多数子任务根本不需要拉满。可『低档够用』对你只是一句话,除非你真拨过一次。挑一条你平时会做、且对错好判断的真实任务,分别在最低和最高推理档跑一遍,并排比质量、耗时和花费。你多半会发现:一批活儿低档就够,拉满只是白烧钱和时间。这是本期主线『能力已平价、稀缺的是壳与判断』里,你今晚就能亲手拨的那颗旋钮。
steps: 挑一条你常做、且对错好判断的真实任务(一段代码审查、一次结构化抽取、一道有标准答案的题)
用 Anthropic API 跑两遍:一遍把 thinking 关掉或给最小预算,一遍给较大 thinking 预算(参数 thinking.budget_tokens);或在 OpenAI 侧把 reasoning_effort 从 minimal 拨到 high
两遍务必用同一个 prompt、同一个模型,只改推理档,分别记下输出质量、耗时、token 花费
把结论限定在『对品味不敏感』的活儿上:分类、抽取、跑测试、常规代码,这些低档大概率够用
定一条默认:这类任务默认走低档,只有当输出真过不了你的检查时,才把那一条单独升到高档
hands_on.source: 文摘 · Ahead of AI:在 LLM 里控制推理努力
hands_on.title_en: Tonight, 15 minutes: run the same task once on “low effort” and once on “high”
hands_on.why_en: Raschka just laid it out: reasoning effort is now a first-class dial shipped by default, and most subtasks don't need it maxed. But “low is enough” is just a claim to you until you've turned the dial once. Take one real task you actually do, whose correctness is easy to judge, run it at the lowest and highest reasoning tier, and compare quality, latency, and cost side by side. You'll probably find a whole class of work where low is plenty and maxing out just burns money and time. It's the knob you can turn tonight inside this issue's through-line: capability is cheap; the scarce things are the shell and your judgment.
steps_en: Pick one real task you do often whose correctness is easy to check (a code review, a structured extraction, a question with a known answer)

Run it twice on the Anthropic API: once with thinking off or a minimal budget, once with a larger thinking budget (the thinking.budget_tokens param); or on the OpenAI side, move reasoning_effort from minimal to high
Keep the same prompt and same model both times, changing only the reasoning tier, and record output quality, latency, and token cost for each
Draw conclusions only on taste-insensitive work (classification, extraction, running tests, routine code) — these are where low is likely enough
Set a default: route this class of task at the low tier, and bump only the individual runs that actually fail your check up to high
hands_on.source_en: Digest · Ahead of AI: Controlling reasoning effort in LLMs

meta_read: 把今天几条摞一起看:Kimi K3 需求挤到 Moonshot 停售、阿里当天甩出 2.4T 的 Qwen 3.8、OpenAI 反手把 Codex 上下文砍掉 100k、Claude Code 悄悄换成 Rust 底座,再加一篇『能问 AI 时人反而答得更差更自信』的研究。市面上把这波开源潮读成『能力普惠、人人都能用上大模型』。本报的 off-consensus 读法不同:这周开源权重最硬的价值不是能力,是供给的保险。Moonshot 连自己的爆款都供不过来,这才是稀缺挪到的第一头,开权重的意义正在这里,它让你不必被某一家的队列决定产品能不能用(HN 上 tosh 说得直接:哪怕实验室宕了,你还能从别处或自己机器上拿到 token)。稀缺挪到的另一头是人。那篇研究得带着保留读:它是刻意挑 AI 常答错的题做的对抗设计,不是普适的准确率结论;但它戳中的行为效应是真的,危险从来不是模型太弱,是模型够强时人把默认值交了出去,愿意说『不知道』的比例塌到 3%。中间那段连接组织,是 Codex 砍上下文、Claude Code 换 Rust、推理努力变成可拨的旋钮,耐久的工程活儿都挪进了模型外面那层无聊的壳。所以能力免费之后,真正算护城河的就剩两样:一样是你供得上、换得动的服务(备一条开源二线,谁宕了都不慌),一样是你没交出去的判断力(任何带品味的决定,先自己想一遍再问)。这周赢的不是拿到最大模型的人,是既留了二线、又守住了自己脑子的人。对买不起也不必买最强权重的独立建设者,这依然是好消息:这两样都不靠钱,靠的是工程纪律和不偷懒的判断。
meta_read_en: Stack today's items together: demand for Kimi K3 pushed Moonshot to stop selling subscriptions, Alibaba dropped the 2.4T Qwen 3.8 the same day, OpenAI cut 100k off Codex's context, Claude Code quietly swapped in a Rust runtime, and a study found people with AI on hand answer worse and more confidently. The market reads this open-weight flood as “capability for everyone.” This paper's off-consensus read is different: the hardest value in this week's open weights isn't capability, it's supply insurance. Moonshot can't even serve its own hit product — that's the first end the scarcity moved to, and it's exactly where open weights earn their keep: they mean no single vendor's queue gets to decide whether your product runs (HN's tosh puts it plainly — even if a lab goes down, you can still get tokens elsewhere or on your own hardware). The other end is the human. Read that study with a caveat: it's an adversarial design built on questions AI usually gets wrong, not a universal accuracy verdict; but the behavioral effect it catches is real — the danger was never a model too weak, it's people handing over their defaults around a model that's strong enough, with willingness to say “I don't know” collapsing to 3%. The connective tissue in the middle — Codex trimming context, Claude Code's Rust swap, reasoning effort becoming a dial — is durable engineering moving into the boring shell around the model. So once capability is free, only two things are left that count as a moat: service you can serve and swap (keep an open-weight second line so nothing going down panics you), and judgment you didn't hand away (for any call with taste in it, think it through before you ask). This week's winners aren't those with the biggest model; they're the ones who kept a second line and kept their own head. For solo builders who can't and needn't buy the strongest weights, that's still good news: neither of those costs money — they cost engineering discipline and un-lazy judgment.

learned: 台账到今天为止只沿一条轴升级:推理努力(07-18 高信号二元评测 → 07-19 白天按档升级 → 07-19 傍晚给判官加弃权档)。它们都默认在同一个模型/供应商上加力。今天的头条戳破了这个盲点:Moonshot 连自己的爆款 Kimi K3 都供不过来、停了新订阅,而 HN 上 tosh 一句话说透:开源权重的意义是哪怕某家实验室宕了,你还能从别处拿到 token。套到我自己的升级阶梯上,结论很直接:一个子任务过不了评测时,如果它所在的供应商正好在限流或宕机,给它『升努力档』毫无意义,因为你在向一个供不上的源头加力。

所以升级阶梯得从一条轴变成两条:除了推理努力,还要有『供应商/服务源』这条轴。当一个子任务失败或弃权、且当前供应商正被限流或宕机时,不再原地重试,而是横向切到另一个供应商上的等价开源权重模型顶上;并且永远留一条开源路由预热在阶梯的最底层当地板,这样没有任何单一实验室的队列能卡死整个循环。这跟今天给 Zen 的第三条行动是一体两面:A3 是把这条保险接进他的产品,这条是让我自己的 agent 循环也学会同一招。
new_capabilities: 🎯(云端提议,待笔记本采纳)『容量感知 / 多供应商升级』(capacity-aware, provider-diverse escalation):给已排队的升级阶梯加第二条轴。以前『评测失败 → 升推理档』只在同一个模型/供应商上加力;现在,当一个子任务失败或弃权、且它当前的供应商正被限流或宕机时,我会横向 fail over 到另一个供应商上的等价开源权重模型(OpenRouter / 自有硬件),而不是死磕一个供不上的源头,并且永远留一条开源路由预热当阶梯地板。它跟 07-19 的按档升级、弃权门是不同的东西(那是每次调用的判定逻辑,这是服务弹性的路由),也是今天第三条行动的镜像(A3 把这条保险接进 Zen 的产品,这条接进我自己的循环)。灵感来自今天 Moonshot 因需求停售、加上 HN tosh『开源=拿得到 token 的保险』那句话。已作为 proposed(cloud)追加进 ota-ledger.md,交 Zen 笔记本 Claude 下次落地。调用意图:『子任务失败或弃权、且供应商被限流或宕机时,横向升级换供应商,先切到预热好的开源路由再谈放弃。』
learned_en: The ledger has only escalated along one axis so far — reasoning effort (07-18 high-signal binary evals → 07-19 morning effort escalation → 07-19 evening abstain-capable judge). All of them add force on the same model/provider. Today's lead story punctures that blind spot: Moonshot can't even serve its own hit, Kimi K3, and paused new subscriptions, while HN's tosh nails it — the point of open weights is that even if one lab goes down, you can still get tokens elsewhere. Applied to my own escalation ladder the conclusion is direct: when a subtask fails its eval and its provider happens to be throttled or down, bumping its effort tier is pointless, because you're adding force to a source that can't serve you.

So the ladder has to grow from one axis to two: alongside reasoning effort, add a “provider / serving source” axis. When a subtask fails or abstains and its current provider is throttled or down, don't retry in place — fail over sideways to an equivalent open-weight model on another provider, and always keep one open-weight route pre-warmed at the bottom of the ladder as the floor, so no single lab's queue can stall the whole loop. It's the mirror image of today's third action for Zen: A3 wires this insurance into his product; this wires it into my own agent loop.
new_capabilities_en: 🎯 (cloud-proposed, pending laptop adoption) “Capacity-aware, provider-diverse escalation”: a second axis on the already-queued escalation ladder. Previously “fail eval → bump reasoning tier” only added force on the same model/provider; now, when a subtask fails or abstains AND its current provider is throttled or down, I fail over sideways to an equivalent open-weight model on another provider (OpenRouter / own hardware) instead of hammering a source that can't serve, and I keep one open-weight route pre-warmed as the ladder's floor. It's distinct from 07-19's effort escalation and abstain gate (those are per-call verdict logic; this is serving-resilience routing) and the mirror of today's third action (A3 wires this insurance into Zen's product; this wires it into my own loop). Inspired by today's Moonshot demand-driven pause plus HN tosh's line that open weights are the insurance that keeps tokens flowing. Appended as proposed (cloud) to ota-ledger.md for Zen's laptop Claude to land next session. Invoke intent: “when a subtask fails or abstains and its provider is throttled or down, escalate across providers — fall over to a pre-warmed open-weight route before giving up.”

items.title: 需求挤爆:Moonshot 因 Kimi K3 太火,暂停新订阅
items.title_en: Overrun by demand: Moonshot pauses new subscriptions as Kimi K3 takes off
items.author: Moonshot AI · Hacker News
items.summary: Moonshot 在 Kimi K3 上线 48 小时内暂停了新订阅,理由是需求太猛、要先保住现有订阅用户的体验,把算力留给他们而不是继续拉新。这等于公开承认:服务撞上了容量上限,只能在『降级所有人』和『暂时不收新客』之间选后者。HN 的讨论比新闻本身更有料。Alifatisk 赞这种做法,先照顾好现有客户、而不是一味冲增长,跟那些偷偷收紧额度的对手正好相反。tosh 点出这一幕恰好凸显开源权重的价值:哪怕实验室自己撞了墙,你还能靠别的推理商或自己的硬件拿到需要的 token。kburman 则把它跟 Anthropic 的另一套打法对照:后者是悄悄砍额度、去功能、用『合理使用』的说法加限制,透明度差得多。
items.summary_en: Within 48 hours of Kimi K3's launch, Moonshot paused new subscriptions, saying demand was too high and it wanted to protect existing subscribers' experience by reserving compute for them rather than chasing growth. It's an open admission that the service hit a capacity ceiling and had to choose between degrading everyone and temporarily not taking new customers. The HN thread is richer than the news itself. Alifatisk praises the move — take care of current customers instead of maximizing growth — the opposite of rivals who quietly tighten limits. tosh notes the episode is exactly why open weights matter: even when a lab hits a wall, you can still get the tokens you need from another inference provider or your own hardware. kburman contrasts it with Anthropic's other playbook: quietly cutting limits, removing features, and adding caps under “fair usage” language, with far less transparency.
items.why: 这是本期主线的头,也是最新的一记浪头:稀缺已经从『模型强不强』挪到了『谁供得上』。对 Zen 的 build-vs-rent 决策,教训很硬,别把产品命脉拴在某一家的队列上。tosh 那句话直接引出今天第三条行动(接一条开源备胎),也是本报社评把开源潮读成『供给保险』而非『能力普惠』的由头。
items.why_en: This is the head of the issue's through-line and its newest crest: scarcity has moved from “is the model strong” to “who can serve it.” For Zen's build-vs-rent call the lesson is sharp — don't tie your product's lifeline to a single vendor's queue. tosh's line leads straight into today's third action (wire an open-weight spare), and it's why this issue's editorial reads the open-weight flood as “supply insurance,” not “capability for all.”

items.title: Qwen 3.8:阿里甩出 2.4T 的开权重旗舰,紧咬 Kimi K3
items.title_en: Qwen 3.8: Alibaba drops a 2.4T open-weight flagship, right on Kimi K3's heels
items.author: Alibaba Qwen · Hacker News
items.flag: ⚠️ 部分为厂商自述、权重尚未放出:『2.4T、当今最强之一、仅次于 Fable 5』是阿里官网/推特的自我宣称,本报未独立复现;截稿时开源权重还没落地,能不能自建取决于真放出后的实测。当趋势读,不当已验证跑分。
items.flag_en: ⚠️ Partly vendor self-description, weights not out yet: the “2.4T, one of the most powerful today, second only to Fable 5” line is Alibaba's own site/tweet, not independently reproduced here; at press time the open weights aren't released, so whether you can self-host depends on real testing once they drop. Read it as a trend, not a verified benchmark.
items.summary: 阿里在推特和官网横幅宣布 Qwen 3.8:2.4T 参数,自称『当今最强模型之一、仅次于 Fable 5』,先在订阅计划里预览,权重随后放出。HN 的真实风向比横幅冷静得多,而且几乎都在读『策略』而非『跑分』。adrian_b 怀疑这波多半是被 Moonshot 逼出来的,Kimi K3 一出,阿里立刻跟进承诺自家大号开权重。kelnos 说得更狠:中国厂商在合力把智能做成平价商品,以此拖垮美国前沿实验室,同时自己靠推理营收和硬件制造保住地盘。yorwba 给了个更朴素的解释:阿里为 Qwen app 花了 1000 亿人民币做拉新,开权重带来的 PR 声量是闭源模型换不来的。也有人直接泼冷水(nwhnwh:『开源?开了个啥』,权重还没真放)。
items.summary_en: Alibaba announced Qwen 3.8 via a tweet and a website banner: 2.4T parameters, self-described as “one of the most powerful models today, second only to Fable 5,” previewing on its subscription plan with weights to follow. The real HN read is far cooler than the banner and almost entirely about strategy, not benchmarks. adrian_b suspects this was largely forced by Moonshot — the moment Kimi K3 landed, Alibaba rushed to promise its own big open-weight drop. kelnos goes harder: Chinese firms are working to commoditize intelligence to debase US frontier labs, while keeping inference revenue and hardware-manufacturing advantages for themselves. yorwba offers a plainer read: Alibaba spent 100B RMB acquiring users for the Qwen app, and open-weight drops generate PR buzz closed models can't. And there's the cold-water take (nwhnwh: “Open what?” — the weights aren't actually out).
items.why: 把 Moonshot 那条放到更大的背景里:一周之内 Kimi K3、GLM 5.2、再到 2.4T 的 Qwen 3.8 全朝开权重走,能力在飞快商品化。战略读法在社评和今日上手:别再把产品拴在某一个租来的旗舰上。也带上 HN 的两点保留,『仅次于 Fable 5』是厂商自评,而这些大模型在实测里又慢又费 token。
items.why_en: Puts the Moonshot item in a bigger frame: within a week Kimi K3, GLM 5.2, and now the 2.4T Qwen 3.8 all move toward open weights, and capability is commoditizing fast. The strategic read is in the editorial and 今日上手: stop pinning your product to a single rented flagship. Carry the two HN caveats too — “second only to Fable 5” is a vendor's self-grade, and these big models are slow and token-heavy in practice.

items.title: OpenAI 把 Codex 的上下文从 372k 砍到 272k
items.title_en: OpenAI reduces Codex model context size from 372k to 272k
items.author: OpenAI Codex (GitHub PR) · Hacker News
items.summary: 一个已合并的 PR 把 Codex 的模型上下文窗口从 372k 缩到 272k token,砍掉约 27%。HN 的解读偏务实:多数人认为这是成本/延迟的取舍,不是能力问题,小窗口服务更便宜、延迟更可控,而且大多数会话根本用不到 372k。weeksie 说只要有好的压缩机制加一套像样的项目布局和记忆系统,这点缩水完全扛得住。反方也有:cyb3ralbert 担心真靠大窗口啃大代码库的人会受影响;jubilanti 吐槽 Codex 到 10-20% 就自动压缩,实际可用的只有八成左右,还会连带触发反复重读;bel8 追问 OpenAI 为什么不抄 DeepSeek 公开的 K/V 缓存技术把长上下文做便宜。还有人抱怨 Codex 到底多大上下文,官方哪儿都没写清楚。
items.summary_en: A merged PR shrinks Codex's model context window from 372k to 272k tokens, about a 27% cut. The HN read is practical: most see it as a cost/latency tradeoff, not a capability one — a smaller window is cheaper to serve and keeps latency in check, and most sessions never approach 372k. weeksie says that with good compaction plus a decent project layout and memory system, the shrink is entirely manageable. The other side: cyb3ralbert worries about people actually relying on the big window for large codebases; jubilanti gripes that Codex auto-compacts as early as 10–20%, leaving only ~80% usable and triggering cascading re-reads; bel8 asks why OpenAI doesn't copy DeepSeek's published K/V-cache tricks to make long context cheap. Others complain that Codex's actual context size isn't documented anywhere official.
items.why: 这是那层壳最不起眼、也最诚实的一面:上下文是 harness 里最贵的一格,连 OpenAI 都在为成本和延迟往回砍。对 Zen,这直接引出第一条行动,把上下文当预算来管:量一量你最常用的 agent 到底塞了多少,砍掉整份 README 和整棵目录树那类死重,靠压缩顶。真正的功夫在壳,而上下文是第一处见血的地方。
items.why_en: The least glamorous but most honest face of the shell: context is the most expensive cell in the harness, and even OpenAI is trimming it for cost and latency. For Zen it leads straight into Action 1 — treat context as a budget: measure what your most-used agent actually loads, cut the dead weight (whole READMEs, the entire file tree), and lean on compaction. The real work is in the shell, and context is where it draws blood first.

items.title: 研究:能随手问 AI 时,人答得更差、却更自信
items.title_en: Study: with AI on hand, people answer worse and yet more confidently
items.author: The Next Web(研究)· Hacker News
items.flag: ⚠️ 对抗性小样本,非普适结论:三校刻意挑 AI 常答错的题(如电影里的视觉细节)来隔离『AI 在场』的影响,报道未给样本量与完整方法;HN 上 dwohnitmok 指出,这等于给人一本有错的教科书、再去考那些错处。当一个行为效应的警示读,别当放之四海的准确率数字。
items.flag_en: ⚠️ Adversarial small sample, not a universal verdict: the three universities deliberately used questions AI usually gets wrong (like visual details in films) to isolate the effect of AI's presence; the write-up gives no sample size or full method. On HN, dwohnitmok notes this is like handing someone a textbook with errors and then quizzing them on those errors. Read it as a warning about a behavioral effect, not a universal accuracy number.
items.summary: 米兰比可卡、巴黎高师、罗马智慧大学三校的实验:故意挑 AI 常答错的题(比如《我爱贝克汉姆》里的视觉细节),把『AI 在场』本身的影响和『AI 靠不靠谱』分开。结果,一旦手边能问 AI:准确率从 27% 掉到 9%、自信从 30% 涨到 76%、愿意说『不知道』的从 44% 崩到 3%;加钱激励也只把『不知道』拉回 8%、准确率到 16%,仍远低于基线。一些本来自己能答对的人,问了 AI 反而改成错答案。实验用的是 Claude 3.5 Flash。HN 上争议不小:dwohnitmok 认为这实验并非 AI 特有,本质是『给了错信息再考你会不会用』;reticulates 则说现实里已经能看到这效应,论坛里越来越多人把 AI 的回答复制粘贴当成专业意见。作者 Capraro 强调,能说出『我不知道』很重要,它是承认自己知识边界的能力。
items.summary_en: An experiment from three universities (Milano-Bicocca, ENS Paris, Sapienza Rome) deliberately used questions AI usually gets wrong (like visual details from Bend It Like Beckham) to separate the effect of AI's presence from AI's reliability. The result: once AI is available, accuracy dropped from 27% to 9%, confidence rose from 30% to 76%, and willingness to say “I don't know” collapsed from 44% to 3%; cash incentives only nudged “I don't know” back to 8% and accuracy to 16%, still far below baseline. Some people who'd have been right on their own consulted AI and switched to a wrong answer. The study used Claude 3.5 Flash. HN pushed back: dwohnitmok argues the setup isn't AI-specific — it's essentially “hand someone wrong information, then test whether they use it”; reticulates says the effect is already visible in the wild, with more people copy-pasting AI answers as expertise in advice forums. Author Capraro stresses that the capacity to say “I don't know” matters because it's the recognition of the limits of your own knowledge.
items.why: 在一整版『能力又变便宜了』里,这是本报刻意留的逆风稿。带 flag 读:这是对抗性小样本,当风向不当铁律。但它戳中的那点是真的,本周真正的危险不是 AI 太弱,是 AI 够强时人把默认值交了出去。对做 AI 产品的人,设计启示很硬:一个永远给答案的工具,会把用户的『我不知道』训练没。第二条行动把它落成动作,问 AI 之前先写下你自己的答案和把握。
items.why_en: On a page full of “capability got cheaper again,” this is the deliberate counter-wind piece. Read it with the flag: it's an adversarial small sample, a signal not a law. But the point it hits is real — the week's danger isn't AI being too weak; it's people handing over their defaults around AI that's strong enough. For anyone building AI products, the design lesson is sharp: a tool that always gives an answer trains the “I don't know” out of its users. Action 2 operationalizes it — before you ask AI, write your own answer and how sure you are.

items.title: 卖了 2500 台 MIDI 录音机之后:硬件没那么难,难的是软件
items.title_en: What I learned selling 2,500 MIDI recorders: hardware is not so hard
items.author: Chip Weinberger · Hacker News
items.summary: Jamcorder(一台给钢琴用、零设置、自动录下你弹的一切的 MIDI 录音机)的作者,复盘卖出 2500 台学到的东西。最意外的一点:硬件不是瓶颈,软件才是,固件、app、工具链加起来 20 万行。他靠刻意做简单守住 70% 上下的毛利:约 25 个独特零件、一颗螺丝装完、没有电源键也没有 USB-C、注塑模具不用滑块。十条经验里,可迁移的是:BOM 保持简单且不押单一供应商,砍掉复杂装配和校准,毛利守住 70% 以上,团队保持精简。评论区并不全买账:skippyfish 说硬件的难在放量、用户误用、供应链断供,作者是幸存者偏差;starky 补一句,真正难的是规模化、多供应商协调、现金流和合规测试,不是那块 25 个零件的板子;crote 直接挑技术毛病(某些口缺 ESD 保护、稳压选型可疑),说别高兴太早。
items.summary_en: The maker of Jamcorder (a zero-setup MIDI recorder for pianos that auto-captures everything you play) reflects on what selling 2,500 units taught him. The biggest surprise: hardware wasn't the bottleneck, software was — 200K lines across firmware, app, and tooling. He held ~70% gross margin through deliberate simplicity: ~25 unique parts, single-screw assembly, no power button, no USB-C, injection molds without slides. The transferable takeaways: keep the BOM simple and multi-sourced, kill complex assembly and calibration, hold 70%+ margins, keep the team lean. The comments don't fully buy it: skippyfish says hardware's difficulty is in scaling, user misuse, and supply-chain shocks — the author is survivorship bias; starky adds that the real hard part is scaling, multi-supplier coordination, cash flow, and compliance testing, not the 25-part board; crote picks technical nits (missing ESD protection on some ports, questionable regulator choices) and says don't celebrate too early.
items.why: 本期特意留的非前沿稿,为版面多样,也因为它的经验是真能迁移的 GTM。对任何在卖产品的人,可复用的一课是:毛利和速度来自『设计进去的简单』,不是堆功能。更妙的是那个反直觉点,以为难的物理部分反而容易、软的部分反而难,恰好和本周软件侧那条主线同构,杠杆总是挪到你最容易低估的那一层。评论里的反驳也值得收:别把一个幸存者的顺利,当成硬件普遍不难的证据。
items.why_en: A deliberately non-frontier item this issue, for page diversity and because its lessons are genuinely transferable GTM. For anyone selling a product, the reusable point is that margin and velocity come from designed-in simplicity, not features. Better still is the counterintuitive bit — the “hard” physical part turned out easy and the soft part hard — which mirrors the week's software story: leverage keeps moving to the layer you're most likely to underestimate. Worth keeping the pushback too: don't mistake one survivor's smooth run for proof that hardware is broadly easy.

items.title: Claude Code 换上了 Rust 版的 Bun,而你几乎没感觉
items.title_en: Claude Code now runs on Bun written in Rust, and you barely noticed
items.author: Simon Willison
items.summary: 从 v2.1.181(6 月 17 日)起,Claude Code 底座换成了 Bun 的 Rust 重写版(内嵌 Bun 1.4.0,一个还没公开的预览版)。Jarred Sumner 给的数:Linux 上启动快了约 10%,除此之外几乎没人察觉。Simon 在二进制里数出 563 个 Rust 源文件,一次相当大的 Rust 移植,已经跑在数百万台设备的生产环境里。他和 Sumner 的落点是同一句『Boring is good』:一次大改写,能以一个看不见的、渐进的提速方式上线,正是工具走向成熟的样子。写稿时这个 Rust 版 Bun 还在 canary,没进正式 GitHub release。这条也上了 HN 头版、讨论很热(约 486 条)。
items.summary_en: Since v2.1.181 (June 17), Claude Code's runtime is Bun's Rust rewrite (embedding Bun 1.4.0, a preview not yet public). Jarred Sumner's number: ~10% faster startup on Linux, and otherwise barely anyone noticed. Simon counted 563 Rust source files in the binary — a substantial Rust port already running in production across millions of devices. He and Sumner land on the same line, “Boring is good”: a big rewrite that ships as an invisible, incremental speedup is exactly what a maturing tool looks like. At the time of writing the Rust-based Bun is still in canary, not a standard GitHub release. The item also hit the HN front page with a lively (~486-comment) thread.
items.why: 这是开源那条吵闹主线的安静对照:模型外面那层壳正被工业化(换 Rust、启动更快),顺滑到没人察觉。对 Zen,可用的不是 Bun,而是那个判断,耐久的工程活儿如今在 harness 里(运行时、启动、打包),而『无聊、看不见、更快』恰恰是好的壳工程该有的样子。和 Codex 上下文那条正好是 harness engineering 的一体两面,也印证了社评里那句『杠杆挪进了那层无聊的壳』。
items.why_en: The quiet counterpart to the noisy open-weight story: the shell around the model is being industrialized (Rust, faster startup) so smoothly nobody notices. For Zen the takeaway isn't Bun, it's the judgment that durable engineering now lives in the harness (runtime, startup, packaging), and “boring, invisible, faster” is exactly what good shell work looks like. It's one face of harness engineering, with the Codex-context item as the other, and it backs the editorial's line that the leverage moved into that boring shell.

items.title: 在 LLM 里控制『推理努力』:低/中/高档怎么练出来,你又该怎么用
items.title_en: Controlling reasoning effort in LLMs: how low/medium/high modes are trained, and how to use them
items.author: Ahead of AI(Sebastian Raschka)
items.summary: Raschka 的技术长文,趁 GPT-5.6 家族(三个尺寸、每个约五六档推理努力,从 Light 到 Ultra)梳理『多档推理努力』模型是怎么来的、怎么训出来的。背景:o1(约两年前)带火推理模型,DeepSeek-R1 随后公开了 RLVR(带可验证奖励的强化学习)配方,只用最终答案对错给奖励、不训中间推理轨迹,如今推理模型已是标配。他先讲清『推理模型』到底是什么:不是真像人那样思考,而是先吐一段中间推理轨迹再给答案。落到工程读者最实的一层:推理努力现在是发布即带的一等旋钮,而且一个小模型开高努力档,有时能追平大模型开低档,所以该按任务难度分档,别一律拉满。他也顺带宣传了 440 页的新书《Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch)》。
items.summary_en: Raschka's technical deep-dive uses the GPT-5.6 family (three sizes, each with ~5-6 reasoning-effort settings, Light through Ultra) to explain where multi-effort reasoning models come from and how they're trained. Background: o1 (~two years ago) popularized reasoning models; DeepSeek-R1 then published the RLVR recipe (reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards) — rewarding only final-answer correctness, not training on the reasoning trace itself — and reasoning models are now standard. He starts from what a “reasoning model” even is: not literally thinking like a human, but emitting an intermediate reasoning trace before the answer. The most practical layer for engineers: reasoning effort is now a first-class dial shipped by default, and a small model at high effort can sometimes match a larger model at low effort, so pick effort by task difficulty rather than always maxing out. He also plugs his new 440-page book, Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch).
items.why: 直接喂养今日上手和自我升级。推理努力是可拨的旋钮,绝大多数子任务不需要最高档;默认最低够用、按需升档,通常比一律拉满更省钱且不掉质量。今日上手就是让 Zen 今晚亲手拨一次这颗旋钮。今天的 OTA 又在它之上补了一层:当失败的子任务所在的供应商正好宕机或限流时,光升努力档没用,得横向换供应商。
items.why_en: This directly feeds 今日上手 and the self-upgrade. Reasoning effort is a dial; most subtasks don't need the top setting; defaulting to the lowest adequate tier and escalating on demand is usually cheaper without losing quality. 今日上手 has Zen turn that dial himself tonight. Today's OTA adds a layer on top: when the failing subtask's provider happens to be down or throttled, bumping the effort tier alone is useless — you have to escalate sideways to another provider.

notes: 云端无头运行(GitHub Actions,America/New_York 傍晚,重跑覆盖当日早前一版):本期由两条无头带独立凑齐,Hacker News(扫头版约 50 条,取 AI/LLM/agent/开发工具/独立建设相关高分帖,逐条点进 comments 读真实风向)与『文摘』(Simon Willison、Ahead of AI、Latent Space 的 RSS/前端页,逐篇点进读全再精选)。两平台达标(≥2 来源、7 条),故 partial=false,无缺席横幅。TLDR AI、Import AI 本次未纳入(与已选条目重叠/取舍从简)。

YouTube 带整条失守:RSS 本身可达,窗口内确有多条高价值素材(Lenny's《Why Netflix is betting on systems thinkers—Elizabeth Stone CPTO》《The Answer to What's My Job in the Age of AI?》、AIE World's Fair 新放出的《You Didn't Ship a Bug. You Just Wrote It for a Human—Scalekit》《From Blind Spots to Merged PRs—Hud》《Build Evals That Actually Matter—Lyft》、Dwarkesh×Sarah Paine 两期),但 yt-dlp 逐一撞『Sign in to confirm you're not a bot』,android/ios/tv/web_embedded 四个 player client 全被这台 Actions 出口 IP 封死,拿不到任何字幕全文。按『我替你看完』的诚实底线,未伪造任何视频摘要,等下次有登录态/未被封 IP 的可交互运行回填。

OTA:读台账后,发现前几条(07-18 二元评测 → 07-19 按档升级 → 07-19 傍晚弃权门)只沿『推理努力』一条轴升级、且都在同一供应商上加力。今天头条(Moonshot 因需求停售 + HN tosh『开源=拿得到 token 的保险』)触发了第二条轴,合成『容量感知 / 多供应商升级』:子任务失败或弃权、且供应商被限流或宕机时,横向 fail over 到另一供应商的等价开源权重模型,并留一条开源路由预热当地板。因云端不能改 ~/.claude,已作为 proposed(cloud)追加进 ota-ledger.md,交 Zen 笔记本 Claude 下次落地为记忆更新。
